simple.meaning: קָלַהּ (qâlahh) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to assemble.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 1 time in 2 Samuel, beginning at 2 Samuel 20:14. The surrounding contexts include Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to קָלַהּ (H7035) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: קָלַהּ (qâlahh) / H7035 is traced through 2 Samuel 20:14 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H7035. qalah קלהּ 2Sam 20:14 Kt, see קהל p.874.

occurrences.englishText: He went through all the tribes of Israel to Abel, and to Beth Maacah, and all the Berites. They were gathered together, and went also after him.
